title.narrative: ROAF/KEN/Nairobi Rivers Basin Regeneration - Connecting the city and its people with the rivers in Nairobi: A catalyst to Inclusive Urban Regeneration through efficient multi-level stakeholder engagement

description.narrative: The Nairobi Rivers Basin is a distinctive ecosystem consisting of several rivers including the Nairobi River, Mathare River and Ngong River, and a mix of forests and savanna grasslands, key green public spaces, a large national park, wetland areas and several significant urban forests. However, in recent years, there has been a dramatic decrease in natural assets and green coverage by an estimated 20% across Nairobi, resulting in a decline in the larger river ecosystem. These rivers have significantly suffered from the ‘triple planetary crises' of climate change, nature and biodiversity loss, and pollution, with many of the settlements along the rivers being at risk due to their location in flood-prone areas. These intertwined challenges have cumulatively led to environmental degradation, increased loss of biodiversity, public health concerns, and a decline in the overall quality of life of the residents, coupled with significant effects from climate change. There is therefore a need for urgent action to regenerate these rivers. The rising interest in the regeneration of the rivers of Nairobi amongst stakeholders in the recent past provides a unique opportunity to kick start the process, leveraging on the political will and commitment, led from the highest level of Government, the President and the Deputy President, as an unparalleled chance to convene stakeholders and demonstrate inclusive participation in the rivers regeneration. The Nairobi Rivers Commission was established by the President of the Republic of Kenya on 2nd December 2022, through a gazette notice that underscored the State’s role in protecting the environment, mitigating environmental degradation, combatting the devastating impacts of climate change, and enhancing protection of biodiversity. The commission is mandated to protect and restore the ecological integrity of Nairobi's rivers through a basin-wide approach that ensures their sustainability and improves the quality of life of the communities living along the waterways. It is key for the Commission to work with various stakeholders, including government agencies, NGOs, the private sector, development and multi-lateral partners and more significantly the river line communities, to achieve its goals and promote building consensus, collaboration, and alignment of the efforts with the needs and aspirations of the communities they serve.
